entries.description: A land trust holding 145 acres in southern Oregon, welcoming all women and children to live there or visit. Type is Land Trust because it explicitly states putting land in a land trust. Acreage is 145. Accepted groups: 'all women and children' in 1976 prose directory includes Lesbian women, Non-lesbian women, Girl children, Boy children.
entries.raw_text: LAND TRUSTS FOR WOMEN is an effort to give women control over their own destinies. Two groups of women have researched the concept of land trusts, and formed groups to acquire land for all women and children at all times. This would promote the spiritual, emotional, physical, cultural, and economic well-being of women, and preserve the land. Many of us love nature deeply, and need to live with green all around us and be self-sufficient. We feel caged in polluted, violent cities where we survive day to day by doing meaningless work or by standing in welfare lines. Financially poor women are unable to buy rural property. Private ownership creates hassles anyway. Putting land in a land trust removes it from the speculative market. It would be available to all women and children, whether they want to live there or just stop for a short time, camp out, and relax. We can help women set up local land trusts, or they can join us. Oregon Women's Land Trust has bought 145 acres in southern Oregon. Write OWLT, Box 1713, Eugene, OR, 97401, or California Women's Land Trust, c/o Carole & Yolanda, 1538 N. St. Andrews, Hollywood, CA, 90028.
entries.notes: Listed jointly with California Women's Land Trust in the same paragraph; separated into two rows per codebook. Type is Land Trust based on 'Putting land in a land trust'. Acreage is 145. Accepted groups inferred from 'all women and children'.

entries.description: A group with 80 acres in northwest Arkansas, aiming to form a women's land trust. Type is Land Trust based on 'form a women's land trust'. Acreage is 80. Accepted groups: 'live only with dykes' gives Lesbian women; 'relate to female children only' gives Girl children. Focuses: farming ('stress farming... to raise food') and lesbian separatism ('We will live only with dykes').
entries.raw_text: WOMEN ON LAND has "secured" 80 acres of land in northwest Arkansas as a beginning for a women's land trust. We are investigating and researching the details of how to form a land trust. We believe a land trust is a way each woman involved with this land can have equal access and responsibility to the land to the feminist community. The concept of a land trust can take care of legal trips and power trips. The land can be legally "owned" by the land trust and each woman could have lease for lifetime use of the land. There is much to be worked out, but we want to know that no woman woman will get ripped off after putting in her time, energy, work, or money. It is difficult to review all the research and energy into laws, qualifying to fit their rules, and at the same time, trying to build a new culture, but we have to use their laws for some measure of protection against them. We will live only with dykes. We wish to relate to female children only - male children would be too sexist an influence on a developing women's environment. We want to stress farming on this land to raise food to feed the women on the land and support sisters in the cities. There are no buildings on the land, just 80 acres of beautiful trees, a waterfall, a creek, and lots of painful bugs. We need to share the responsibility for getting money to pay off the land, for gathering tools, building materials, seed, horse, windmill. We are open to any woman who wants to relate to this land whether she wants to stay full-time, work for the summer, camp and work, spend the weekend, or stay here on the way cross country. We do want to emphasize the need to work. When you write, describe yourself, your politics, what you can offer and why you want to come. (No dogs please.) Send a stamped, self-addressed envelope to Women on Land, PO Box 521, Fayetteville, Arkansas, 72701.
entries.notes: Type is Land Trust ('women's land trust'). Acreage is 80. Accepted groups: Lesbian women ('live only with dykes') and Girl children ('relate to female children only'). Focuses: Farming/self-sufficiency ('stress farming on this land to raise food') and Lesbian separatism ('We will live only with dykes').

entries.land_location_as_stated: eastern foothills of the Cascade mountains in Washington
entries.description: A small lesbian farm in the eastern foothills of the Cascade mountains in Washington rebuilding an old farm valley. Type is Intentional Community/Cooperative because residents and visitors are living and working on the land. Accepted groups: visitors include 'two women and one child, with many visitors', so Lesbian women, Non-lesbian women, Girl children, Boy children. Focuses: Workshops/education ('workshops on health', 'School' in name) and Environmentalism/eco-friendly ('presently open to the sky and a valley view, stream water is pumped').
entries.raw_text: SAPPHA SURVIVAL SCHOOL is a small lesbian farm in the eastern foothills of the Cascade mountains in Washington. One woman who stayed there for a week last summer wrote the following about SSS. "Two women and one child, with many visitors, started this spring to rebuild an old farm valley into a place for all women to work and live, or visit. I helped rebuild the old cabin, later to be the community center, helped dig a well, and build a chicken coop. Freedom and Dykepride run strong - the valley is isolated enough to remove society's inhibitions and its censure of lesbians. Olivia Newton Outhouse is presently open to the sky and a valley view, stream water is pumped to flow between branches for the shower and half naked Amazons are everywhere! Evening relaxation is often a sauna, fueled by hot rocks and followed by a dip in the stream." This summer they planned on more structures including a children's space scaled to their size, and an outrageous playground scaled to everybody's size. They also planned an herb garden, a festival in June, and workshops on health. To find out more, write: SSS, Box 4D, Aeneaes Valley Road, Tonasket, WA, 98855.
entries.notes: Type is Intentional Community/Cooperative ('rebuild an old farm valley into a place for all women to work and live'). entries.land_location_as_stated: area of Oklahoma near Tishomingo, capitol of the chicasaw nation
entries.description: A 70-acre land space opening soon in Oklahoma near Tishomingo for recreation, farming, and general growing. Type is Intentional Community/Cooperative as a residential group opening on the land. Acreage is 70. Accepted groups: 'women' in 1976 prose directory includes Lesbian women and Non-lesbian women. Focuses: farming ('farming, and general growing', 'community garden will be the major food source') and environmentalism ('cooperative energy').
entries.raw_text: ANOTHER DEMENTION is opening soon to accomodate women who are seeking a space on the land working together with other women in areas of recreation, farming, and general growing. 70 acres will be available for camping and/or year-round living in beautiful wilderness area of Oklahoma near Tishomingo, capitol of the chicasaw nation. A variety of flora and fauna abound in the area of the wildlife refuge 3 miles away and can be enjoyed while canoeing down the blue river or pennington creek. Wild mustangs adopted through the government will be among the horses in residence eager to offer alternative means of transportation around the area for exploration and enjoyment. Womancraft can be sold in distribution outlet store on roadfront or consigned to be distributed by the MAGIC FERRY to the FERRY DYKINGS and other contact points across the country. Women in residence will maintain their own shelter and be responsible for their own life-support needs. A community garden will be the major food source operating on cooperative energy. Monthly rate for any number of days spent on the land is $5.00, payable on or before each new moon. This money will be used for payment of the land. Financial
